summary: The original is a bright, full-saturation sinusoidal wave sweeping along the cloud's vertical axis whose tilt circles once per 8 s with the synthetic accelerometer; the port renders visually black (peak channel value 2/255 on every frame from t=0 s to t=130 s), and the faint structure it does have is a set of hard-edged planes on the WRONG lattice axis.
observations: Both sides compile and run with no compile/runtime error, both report wantsSensors: true, and both were fed the identical beat120 synthetic feed (meta.json sensors: "synth", sensorModel: "beat120" on orig and port in every run).

PORT IS VISUALLY BLACK. baseline (6 s / 20 fps, cloud 5x5x5): orig meanBrightness avg 50 (min 45, max 61), port meanBrightness avg 0 with min == max == 0 and zeroMotionFrames 120/120. The survey (60 s / 10 fps) is identical: port meanBrightness {avg 0, min 0, max 0}, zeroMotionFrames 600/600. port.png is uniformly black to the eye while orig.png is a dense saturated rainbow waterfall.

The port is not literally dead — it is ~128x too dim. --dump at 0.15/1.25/2.40/3.55/4.65/5.80 s on the default 5x5x5 cloud: orig lights 50-59 of 125 pixels with maxChan 255 and frame sums ~17,400-21,900; port lights 8-21 pixels with maxChan 2 (values only ever 0, 1 or 2) and frame sums 15-42. motionLit on the port sits at ~0.5-0.7 (non-zero, so it IS animating) while motion rounds to 0.

The dimness is the steady state, not a warm-up or a phase. --skip 120 --seconds 10: port still maxChan 2 (lit 12-15 px, mean value 0.12-0.16) at t=120.15/124.35/129.15 s while orig holds maxChan 255 and mean value ~102-104. Unchanged at --fps 10, 40 and 80, at --pixels 1000 (10x10x10 cloud), and at seeds 1, 7 and 1234 — port mean 0 in all nine runs.

ORIGINAL STRUCTURE: a clean k=1 sinusoid along the SLOWEST-varying lattice axis (index/n^2, i.e. height). On the 10x10x10 cloud the per-plane mean value along that axis runs a smooth hump from ~53 to ~155 (k=1 DFT magnitude 22-29) while the two faster axes are nearly flat (per-plane lit counts 40-55, k=1 magnitudes 0-11). Value histogram is strongly bimodal — ~40-50% of pixels railed at 224-255 and the rest at 0, with only 5-15 pixels anywhere in between — i.e. a hard-thresholded band lit in fully saturated rainbow hues.

ORIGINAL MOTION: the crest translates steadily along that vertical axis. De-aliased 0.05 s dumps show the peak plane walking 8 -> 5 -> 3 -> 1 -> 0 -> wrap to 9 -> 8, giving -1.51 cycles/s (period ~0.66 s) — a full traversal of the cube's height roughly every two-thirds of a second. A coarse 0.35 s dump grid reported +1.33 cyc/s, which is the Nyquist alias of the same motion; the fine grid is authoritative.

ORIGINAL ACCELEROMETER COUPLING IS REAL AND MEASURABLE: the wave axis tilts off vertical and the tilt direction rotates in lockstep with the harness's 8-second accelerometer tilt circle. Over a 16.45 s window the k=1 magnitudes along the two horizontal axes oscillate in antiphase with a ~4 s period (twice per 8 s revolution, as a projected sinusoid should): xMag 11.1 at t=0.00 -> 1.5 at 2.10 -> 7.6 at 4.20 -> 0.5 at 6.30 -> 7.1 at 7.70, and 10.8 at t=16.10 (back to its t=0 value one/two revolutions later); yMag peaks at 2.10, 6.30 and 14.00 s. The vertical k=1 magnitude meanwhile holds steady at 22-29 throughout, so the tilt is a modest (up to ~40%) lean on a mostly-vertical wave. The 60 s survey waterfall shows the matching ~7-8 large repeating bands.

The original DEPENDS on the accelerometer: with --sensors off (accel all zero) it renders completely black — 0 lit pixels at every dumped time across a 12 s window, mean 0, motion 0. The port does the opposite.

PORT WITH SENSORS OFF IS ~10x BRIGHTER THAN WHEN FED, which localizes the failure to the accelerometer path. --sensors off --pixels 1000: port lights 300-400 of 1000 pixels at maxChan 18-58 (vs maxChan 2 when fed). So the accel term is what collapses the port's output, not a global brightness constant alone — though even unfed the port peaks ~5-14x below the original's 255.

PORT'S WAVE IS ON THE WRONG AXIS AND THE WRONG SPATIAL FREQUENCY. Unfed at 10x10x10 the port lights whole planes at fixed values of the FASTEST-varying index (index % n) — lit-by-x counts {0,0,100,0,0,100,0,0,100,0} at t=0.15 s, {0,100,0,0,100,0,0,100,0,0} at 2.35 s, {100,0,0,100,0,0,100,0,0,100} at 4.55 s — perfectly uniform (30-40 lit per plane) along both other axes. That is 3-4 sharp planes with a stride of 3, i.e. ~3.3 cycles across the cube, marching along that axis over time. The original puts ONE smooth cycle across the orthogonal (vertical) axis. Same signature on the default 5x5x5 rig: unfed the port lights exactly the 25 pixels with index % 5 == 3, a single plane.
The port's planes are binary, not sinusoidal: pixels are either on the plane or fully off, with no gradient between planes — whereas the original's per-plane profile is a smooth cosine.

When the accelerometer feed IS applied, the port's plane structure dissolves into scattered value-1/2 dust with no coherent axis: per-plane lit counts along the vertical axis go from (20,15,6,3,7,17,20,11,4,5) at t=0.15 s to a flat (10,10,12,11,10,11,10,11,12,10) by t=6.75 s, and the vertical k=1 DFT magnitude is 0.0 at every one of 48 sampled times across a 16.45 s window (vs 21.7-29.0 on the original). Spatial correlation between the sides' per-pixel brightness at matched times is 0.09, -0.06, -0.11, -0.05, 0.03, -0.07 — i.e. none.

Neither side is frame-rate coupled in the pathological sense: the original's brightness is fps-invariant (mean 50-51 at 10/20/40/80 fps) and its motion stat halves with each fps doubling (57 -> 37 -> 20 -> 10), the signature of time-based motion. The port's failure is likewise fps-independent.
Control surfaces MATCH: the probe reports "(no settable controls)" on both orig and port, so there is no dial mismatch and no dialed comparison to make.
Both sides render identically across seeds 1, 7 and 1234 (orig mean 50 / motion 38 in all three; port mean 0 in all three), so the pattern is not RNG-driven and the failure is not a seed fluke.
feedback: Headline: the port's output peaks at channel value 2 out of 255 when the accelerometer is fed — a viewer sees a black rig. Everything below is secondary to fixing that, but the axis bug is independent of it and would still be wrong at correct brightness.

The brightness collapse is specifically in the accelerometer path: unfed (accel = 0) the port peaks at 18-58, fed it peaks at 2, a further ~10-25x loss. Whatever term consumes the accelerometer is scaling the output toward zero instead of steering it. Note the harness feed is a tilt circle of radius 0.2 in x and y with a constant resting z — small horizontal values, so a term that divides by, squares, or normalizes against the horizontal components will vanish exactly like this.

Even with the accelerometer term removed the port is still ~5-14x too dim: it peaks at 18-58 where the original rails at 255 over ~40-50% of the cloud. The original's value distribution is bimodal (a hard threshold: mostly 0 or mostly 224-255), so aim for saturated on/off, not a low-amplitude wash.

WRONG AXIS: the port's wave varies along the fastest-varying pixel index (index % n) — whole planes at fixed x, uniform in y and z. The original's wave varies along the slowest axis (index / n^2, the vertical), uniform in x and y. The wave should propagate up the cloud's height, not sideways along the fastest index. This looks like the height coordinate and the first coordinate being swapped when the 3D position is read.

WRONG SPATIAL FREQUENCY: the port draws 3-4 crests across the cube (planes at a stride of 3 on a 10-deep axis, ~3.3 cycles); the original draws exactly ONE smooth cycle across the full height (k=1, per-plane mean sweeping 53 to 155). Divide the port's spatial frequency by roughly 3.

WRONG PROFILE: the port's crests are binary — a plane is fully lit and its neighbours are fully dark, with nothing in between. The original's crest is a smooth cosine along the height. Replace the hard plane test with a continuous sinusoidal falloff.

TARGET MOTION: the original's crest traverses the full height at ~1.5 cycles/s (period ~0.66 s), measured from 0.05 s dumps; the crest's peak plane walks 8 -> 5 -> 3 -> 1 -> 0 -> 9 -> 8 on a 10-deep cloud, i.e. toward decreasing index along the height axis. Measure any candidate fix at 0.05 s dump spacing — 0.35 s spacing aliases this into an apparent +1.33 cyc/s in the opposite direction.

TARGET ACCELEROMETER BEHAVIOUR: the accelerometer should TILT the wave's propagation axis, not gate its brightness. On the original the horizontal k=1 magnitudes rise and fall in antiphase with a ~4 s period (two per 8 s tilt revolution, peaking around 0-11) while the vertical k=1 magnitude stays pinned at 22-29 — a mostly-vertical wave leaning up to ~40% off vertical as the tilt vector circles. Use those two numbers (horizontal k=1 sweeping 0-11, vertical k=1 steady at 22-29 on a 10x10x10 cloud) as the acceptance test.

The original renders fully black when the accelerometer reads all zeros — that is correct, expected behaviour for this pattern, not something to defend against. The port currently does the reverse (brightest with dead sensors), which is itself a sign the accel term is being applied inverted.

Colour is unjudgeable until brightness is fixed, but for reference the original lights its crest in fully saturated rainbow hues across the whole wheel (per-pixel values railed at 255 in one or two channels — e.g. [189,255,0], [255,0,235] — with meanR/meanG/meanB all in the 43-56 range over the window, so no single hue dominates).
